title: Per-route margin triggerboard and hiring curve
body:
Purpose: quick working workbook to map per-route gross margin triggers to hiring phasing and a 12-month sprint budget. Use this as the canonical team-level decision board for when we (a) add capacity (hire engineers/ops), (b) accelerate Dedicated capacity, or (c) introduce price nudges.

Assumptions (quick):
- Time horizon: next 12 months (Q3 2026 -> Q2 2027).
- Currency: USD.
- Baseline unit: 1M tokens served per month as baseline aggregate for the mapped routes.
- Cost components: GPU inference (incl. amortized reserved), networking, infra ops (SRE/infra eng time), model licensing/weights cache cost, and non-inference variable (storage, logs).
- Average gross margin target: 55% for hosted routes, 45% for low-margin experimental routes.
- Hiring lead times: SWE = 8w, Infra/SRE = 6w, Solutions Eng = 4w.
- Salary assumptions (fully loaded annual): SWE $220k, Infra/SRE $200k, Solutions Eng $150k, Support $95k. Benefits & taxes multiplier: 1.25.

Summary table (scenario snapshots):

| Route | Monthly tokens (baseline) | Price / 1k tokens | Revenue/mo | Cost/mo | Gross margin | Margin trigger (action) | Suggested hires next 3 mo |
| Route-A (API-low-latency) | 1.2M | $3.50 | $4,200 | $1,600 | 62% | margin < 50% -> increase price by 10% or add ded capacity | +1 SWE, +0.5 Infra |
| Route-B (embeddings) | 0.5M | $10.00 | $5,000 | $3,300 | 34% | margin < 40% -> deploy quantization profile or price +15% | +0.25 SWE, +1 Solutions Eng |
| Route-C (batch-rerank) | 0.8M | $1.20 | $960 | $420 | 56% | margin < 45% -> optimize batching/kcache | none immediate |

(Notes: revenue/mo = tokens/1000 * price; cost/mo is modeled from per-token GPU/infra plus fixed share of infra ops)

12-month hiring curve (sketch):
- Month 0 (today): headcount delta planned: SWE +2 (Q3 hires active by month 2), Infra/SRE +1, Solutions Eng +1 (booking customer onboarding), Support +1 (part-time).
- Month 3: If Route-B margin underperforming after product optimizations -> accelerate Dedicated capacity procurement (capex) OR price test +15%. If we choose Dedicated: provision budget ~$90k/month amortized reserve + one Infra hire.
- Month 6: Re-evaluate per-route gross margins. If aggregate gross margin falls below 48% -> hiring freeze on SWE (except critical infra), push price increases across low-usage routes.

Triggerboard (operational rules):
- Soft trigger: margin drops by 5 percentage points relative to rolling 4-week average -> product optimizations prioritized (quantization, caching) and temporary traffic shaping rules applied.
- Hard trigger: margin drops by 10 percentage points OR sustained for 6 weeks -> pricing experiments (A/B price +10% for new signups), and Finance + Sales review for dedicated commit offers.
- Hiring trigger: add new SWE only when 3 of 4 are true: sustained latency SLO misses, backlog > X (tickets metric), revenue weight of impacted routes > 8% total, and margin improvement unlikely by infra-only ops.

Budget slice (quarterly forecast high-level):
- Q3 2026 (current): incremental hires hiring budget = $120k (SWE 1.5 equiv + infra 0.5 equiv pro-rata), dedicated capacity pipeline reserve = $0 (evaluate), margin cushion = 6% of monthly gross.
- Q4 2026: base op cost + new hires run-rate = +$180k/mo incremental if hires complete. Scenario stress: price -15% (route B) -> revenue delta -$750/mo, margin shifts -6pp.
- Q1 2027: contingent capacity buy (if route B still low margin) = $90k/mo amortized to cost. Hiring budget contingency = $240k.

Pricing sensitivity quick table (Route-B example):
- Baseline: price $10 /1k -> revenue/mo $5,000 -> cost/mo $3,300 -> margin 34%
- Price +10% ($11): revenue $5,500 -> margin 40% (+6pp)
- Price +15% ($11.50): revenue $5,750 -> margin 43% (+9pp)
- Price -10% ($9): revenue $4,500 -> margin 26% (-8pp)
- Price elasticity note: we assume short-term inelastic for existing committed customers; new signups sensitive: ~0.25 elasticity estimate.

Headcount cost math (for quick checks):
- SWE fully loaded monthly = 220k * 1.25 / 12 = $22,917/mo
- Infra/SRE monthly = 200k * 1.25 / 12 = $20,833/mo
- Solutions Eng monthly = 150k * 1.25 / 12 = $15,625/mo
- Support monthly = 95k * 1.25 / 12 = $9,896/mo

Example scenario (concrete):
- Problem: Route-B continues to under-index margin after caching/quantized rollout. CPU/GPU ops show 18% higher per-token cost than forecast due to cache miss pattern.
- Proposed immediate actions: price +15% (target new customers +10% hold period 8w), enable model quantization profile Q2 (projected -12% per-token cost), hire 0.5 SWE to implement backend cache optimizations (expected perf within 6w).
- Financial effect (8-week window): price +15% -> incremental revenue ~$750/mo; quantization -> cost savings ~$400/mo; incremental headcount cost (0.5 SWE) = ~$11.5k/mo -> net margin improvement minimal in month 1 but positive by month 3.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need better per-route token-level cost telemetry by model variant (assign to Omar to scope).
- Confirm elasticity by customer cohort (Priya to run A/B test plan with Sales).
- Add dedicated reserve amortization scenarios to capital plan (Daniel to scope vendor quotes).
- Consider temporary feature gating for low-margin routes if margin floor breached while more permanent measures are implemented.

Appendix (quick table export style):
ROUTE,MONTHLY_TOKENS,PRICE_PER_1K,REVENUE_MO,COST_MO,GROSS_MARGIN
Route-A,1200000,3.50,4200,1600,62%
Route-B,500000,10.00,5000,3300,34%
Route-C,800000,1.20,960,420,56%

Notes for reviewers: this is a working doc. Numbers are placeholders for scenario planning and should be validated against telemetry and the cost model (sheet: infra-costing-v3). I want sign-off from Finance + Product on the triggers before we include them in the payroll planner.
